A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SATTC work and contain readable text, equations, two figures and two tables. Both have ten pages ending with references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.5 report original retrieval experiments, component ablations, hubness analyses and evaluations across four EEG encoders, supported by Tables 1–2 and Figure 2.

after.justification: v2 retains the original retrieval experiments, ablations, hubness analyses and evaluations across four EEG encoders in Sections 4.2–4.5.

M1.justification: The subject-adaptive whitening, adaptive CSLS, structural expert and Product-of-Experts fusion procedures in Sections 3.1–3.5 are unchanged.

E1.justification: THINGS-EEG is consistently relabeled THINGS-EEG2, with a replacement dataset citation. Both versions retain the same described coverage of ten subjects and 200 image categories; no change to the represented data, task or test scenarios is reported.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains ATM, the standardized and whitening baselines, fixed-k CSLS and adaptive CSLS. Table 2 retains ATM, EEGNetV4, EEGConformer and ShallowFBCSPNet with the same baseline-versus-SATTC comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the ten-fold LOSO protocol, nested selection using three development subjects, 200-way retrieval, evaluation metrics and training settings. The dataset-name revision introduces no reported protocol change.

E4.justification: The whitening, CSLS and structural-fusion ablations are unchanged, as are Figure 2's subject, hubness and shortlist analyses. The calibration-window experiment and PoE-weight sensitivity findings on page 8 are also retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over LOSO folds and three random seeds and retain the same qualitative statement about standard deviations and stability. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2, Figure 2 and the experimental prose are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports SATTC at 38.4% Top-5 and 14.8% Top-1 in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(28), their mathematical definitions, assumptions and derivations are unchanged. Neither version adds a theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about label-free calibration, retrieval improvement, hubness reduction and encoder independence. Only the benchmark name changes.

C2.justification: The interpretations of whitening, adaptive CSLS and structural fusion are retained. Section 5 preserves the same limitations concerning single-dataset evaluation, handcrafted structural rules, precomputed similarities and batch refinement.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including AdamW, batch size 1024, learning rate 5×10^-4, temperature 1.0, RTX 4090 hardware and the code link. The dataset-reference replacement adds no processing or access instructions.

R1.justification: Reference [7] changes from Grootswagers et al., 'Human EEG recordings for 1,854 concepts presented in rapid serial visual presentation streams,' to Gifford et al., 'A large and rich EEG dataset for modeling human visual object recognition.' This replaces one cited dataset source; the broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: THINGS-EEG becomes THINGS-EEG2 throughout the abstract, body and conclusion, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The narrative, section order and remaining wording are retained apart from line wrapping.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 receive the revised dataset name in their captions, with minor text reflow. Figures, table structures, placement and numerical displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 consistently specifies THINGS-EEG2 and replaces its cited dataset source, making the stated benchmark provenance more precise. This provides a limited documentation and attribution improvement; the methods, empirical evidence and limitations are unchanged.
